sn56.11:0.3: Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta: The Discourse on the Setting in Motion of the Wheel (of Vision) of the Basic Pattern: the Four True Realities for the Spiritually Ennobled Ones
sn56.11:1.1: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī in the Deer Park at Isipatana.
sn56.11:1.2: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus of the group of five thus:
sn56.11:2.1: "Bhikkhus, these two extremes should not be followed by one gone forth (into the homeless life).
sn56.11:2.3: That which is this pursuit of sensual happiness in sense pleasures, which is low, vulgar, the way of the ordinary person, ignoble, not connected to the goal; and that which is this pursuit of self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, not connected to the goal.
sn56.11:2.4: Bhikkhus, without veering towards either of these two extremes, the One Attuned to Reality has awakened to the middle way, which gives rise to vision, which gives rise to knowledge, which leads to peace, to higher knowledge, to full awakening, to Nibbāna.
sn56.11:3.1: "And what, bhikkhus, is that middle way awakened to by the One Attuned to Reality which gives rise to vision, which gives rise to knowledge, which leads to peace, to higher knowledge, to full awakening, to Nibbāna?
sn56.11:3.2: It is just this Noble Eight-factored Path, that is to say,
sn56.11:3.3: right view, right resolve, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right mental unification.
sn56.11:3.4: This, bhikkhus, is that middle way awakened to by the One Attuned to Reality, which gives rise to vision, which gives rise to knowledge, which leads to peace, to higher knowledge, to full awakening, to Nibbāna.
sn56.11:4.1: "Now this, bhikkhus, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the true reality which is pain:
sn56.11:4.2: birth is painful, aging is painful, illness is painful, death is painful; sorrow, lamentation, physical pain, unhappiness and distress are painful; union with what is disliked is painful; separation from what is liked is painful; not to get what one wants is painful; in brief, the five bundles of grasping-fuel are painful.
sn56.11:4.3: "Now this, bhikkhus, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the pain-originating true reality.
sn56.11:4.4: It is this craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and attachment, seeking delight now here now there; that is,
sn56.11:4.5: craving for sense-pleasures, craving for existence, craving for extermination (of what is not liked).
sn56.11:4.6: "Now this, bhikkhus, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the pain-ceasing true reality.
sn56.11:4.7: It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving, the giving up and relinquishing of it, freedom from it, non-reliance on it.
sn56.11:4.8: "Now this, bhikkhus, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the true reality which is the way leading to the cessation of pain.
sn56.11:4.9: It is this Noble Eight-factored Path, that is to say,
sn56.11:4.10: right view, right resolve, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right mental unification.
sn56.11:5.1: "'This, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the true reality of pain': in me, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.
sn56.11:5.2: "Now on this, 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the true reality of pain — is to be fully understood': in me, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.
sn56.11:5.3: "Now on this, 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the true reality of pain — has been fully understood': in me, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.
sn56.11:6.1: "(Likewise,) in me, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge and light, with respect to: 'This, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the pain-originating true reality,'
sn56.11:6.2: 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the pain-originating true reality — is to be abandoned,'
sn56.11:6.3: and 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the pain-originating true reality — has been abandoned.'
sn56.11:7.1: "(Likewise,) in me, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge and light, with respect to: 'This, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the pain-ceasing true reality,'
sn56.11:7.2: 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the pain-ceasing true reality — is to be personally experienced'
sn56.11:7.3: and 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the pain-ceasing true reality — has been personally experienced.'
sn56.11:8.1: "(Likewise,) in me, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge and light, with respect to: 'This, for the spiritually ennobled ones, is the true reality which is the way leading to the cessation of pain,'
sn56.11:8.2: 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the true reality which is the way leading to the cessation of pain — is to be developed,'
sn56.11:8.3: and 'This — for the spiritually ennobled ones, the true reality which is way leading to the cessation of pain — has been developed.'
sn56.11:9.1: "So long, bhikkhus, as my knowledge and seeing of these four true realities for the spiritually ennobled ones, as they really are in their three phases (each) and twelve modes (altogether) was not thoroughly purified in this way, then so long, in the world with its devas, māras and brahmās, in this population with its renunciants and brahmans, its devas and humans, I did not claim to be fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect awakening.
sn56.11:10.1: But when, bhikkhus, my knowledge and vision of these four true realities for the spiritually ennobled ones, as they really are in their three phases and twelve modes was thoroughly purified in this way, then, in the world with its devas, māras and brahmās, in this population with its renunciants and brahmans, its devas and humans, I claimed to be fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect awakening.
sn56.11:10.2: Indeed, knowledge and seeing arose in me:
sn56.11:10.3: 'Unshakeable is the liberation of my mind; this is my last birth: now there is no more renewed existence.'"
sn56.11:10.4: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn56.11:10.5: Elated, the bhikkhus of the group of five delighted in the Blessed One's statement.
sn56.11:11.1: And while this explanation was being spoken, there arose in the venerable Koṇḍañña the dust-free, stainless vision of the Basic Pattern:
sn56.11:11.2: "whatever is patterned with an origination, all that is patterned with a cessation."
sn56.11:12.1: And when the Wheel (of Vision) of the Basic Pattern (of things) had been set in motion by the Blessed One, the earth-dwelling devas raised a cry:
sn56.11:12.2: "At Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Wheel (of Vision) of the Basic Pattern (of things) has been set in motion by the Blessed One, which cannot be stopped by any renunciant or brahman or māra or brahmā or by anyone in the world."
sn56.11:12.3: Having heard the cry of the earth-dwelling devas, the devas of the Four Great Kings raised the same cry.
sn56.11:12.5: Having heard it, the Thirty-three devas took it up,
sn56.11:12.8: then the devas Who Delight in Creating,
sn56.11:12.9: then the devas With Mastery in the Creations of Others,
sn56.11:12.10: and then the devas of the brahmā group.
sn56.11:13.1: Thus at that moment, at that instant, at that second, the cry spread as far as the brahmā world,
sn56.11:13.2: and this ten thousandfold world system shook, quaked, and trembled, and an immeasurable glorious radiance appeared in the world, surpassing the divine majesty of the devas.
sn56.11:14.1: Then the Blessed One uttered this inspiring utterance:
sn56.11:14.2: "the honorable Koṇḍañña has indeed understood! The honorable Koṇḍañña has indeed understood!
sn56.11:14.3: In this way, the venerable Koṇḍañña acquired the name Koṇḍañña Who Has Understood.
